Mina / Susan —

Following up with the implementation details we can commit to operationally. High-level summary first, then a quick checklist you can hand to procurement: 

1) Tenant-level no-train flag: implemented as a tenant config that disables any training telemetry path at ingestion. Enforcement is at the inference gateway; when flag=true, request payloads and responses are write-blocked from any downstream model-improvement pipeline.

2) KV/cache isolation & TTLs: customer KV entries are namespaced per-tenant. For ClearBlue we can set default TTL=0 for interactive prompts (ephemeral) and provide optional longer TTL only if explicitly enabled in writing.

3) Audit logs & evidence: we can provide per-request immutable audit logs (timestamp, model id, sequence length, token counts, routing decision, region, request hash). We will produce a sample CSV extract as part of the evidence bundle.

4) Export paths & residency: nightly SFTP export of raw transcripts (encrypted) to ClearBlue-managed bucket, and an API export on demand. For EU residency we will pin processing to our eu-central-1 fleet and provide KMS attestation indicating keys are in-region.

5) Subprocessors and attestations: we will include our subprocessor list and confirm any 3rd-party model hosting services are subject to the same no-train commitments for your tenant.

Operational checklist (deliverable for Friday):
- runbook: ops-runbook-draft.md (attached)
- sample_audit_extract.csv (will be redacted sample)
- kms-residency-statement.txt
- sftp-connection-instructions.txt

Note: from an engineering perspective we can enable the tenant flag immediately in a staging environment for you to validate; production enablement requires a short config change window (30 min) and a signed amendment to the DPA.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want a live walkthrough.

— Dev

Susan / Mina —

Quick contract note from our side. We propose the following language to be added as an addendum to the DPA: 

"No-Training and Output Rights. Redwood Inference will process Customer data for the sole purpose of providing inference services and will not use Customer data to train, fine-tune, or improve models or model weights. Customer retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs. Redwood will not assert derivative rights on Customer outputs and will only process outputs for operational purposes necessary to provide the agreed services."
If that maps to your expectations, Marissa can circulate a redlined DPA. Two small asks from legal: (1) Confirm whether the "retain ownership" clause needs to reference derivative works specifically; (2) confirm whether ClearBlue requires an escrow-style snapshot of model weights or artifacts upon termination (we usually do not provide that unless contractually required).

Marissa, attaching the proposed redlines (clearblue_dpa_redlines.pdf) for your review and to produce a DocuSign package.
